security_spec.violation_condition: In the FreeBSD kernel, when cpu_switch() or savectx() saves/restores CHERI capability registers (PCC, DDC, CSP, CGP, CTP, and all GPR capability metadata/tags) using an implicitly assumed capability encoding format, but the RVYA25 profile mandates only Zydefaultcap (uycfg.base=0) without specifying the actual encoding layout—if the kernel's struct pcb or trapframe uses a fixed-size capability representation that diverges from the hardware's actual encoding (e.g., 128-bit vs 256-bit capabilities, different tag-bit positions, or different bounds-compression schemes), capability bounds, permissions, or tag bits are silently truncated, widened, or corrupted across context switches.
security_spec.summary: RVYA25 profile mandates Zydefaultcap capability encoding but omits the actual encoding format specification; FreeBSD's context-switch and signal-delivery paths (cpu_switch.S, sendsig, ptrace) rely on knowing the exact in-memory and in-register capability layout to safely save/restore process capability state without privilege-boundary corruption

findings.finding: struct pcb stores all context as plain uint64_t (pcb_ra, pcb_sp, pcb_gp, pcb_tp, pcb_s[12], pcb_x[32][2], pcb_fcsr). No CHERI capability metadata/tag/bounds fields exist, no __capability-qualified fields, and no conditional CHERI compilation guards. The PCB is sized for baseline RV64, not RV64CHERI. This is correct for a non-CHERI kernel — there is no capability encoding to diverge from.

struct trapframe stores all GPRs and CSRs as plain uint64_t. No capability-aware fields for DDC, PCC, or GPR capability metadata. get_mcontext()/set_mcontext() copy trapframe fields to the user-visible mcontext_t struct gpregs which uses __register_t (= __int64_t). No capability encoding divergence is possible because no CHERI registers are represented.

cpu_switch() saves/restores only ra, sp, s[0-11], and conditionally FPE state using plain sd/ld instructions. No save/restore of CHERI capability registers (PCC, DDC, CSP, CGP, CTP) or capability tags/metadata. On baseline RV64 this is complete; CHERI register save/restore would require new infrastructure not present in this tree.
findings.snippet:
sd ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
sd sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)
sd s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(x13)
...
ld ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
ld sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)

findings.finding: savectx() saves ra, sp, tp, gp, s[0-11], and FPE state using plain sd. No CHERI-specific registers are saved. The function is a non-CHERI context dump. Since no CHERI hardware is targeted, there is no implicit encoding assumption at risk.
findings.snippet:
sd ra, (PCB_RA)(a0)
sd sp, (PCB_SP)(a0)
sd tp, (PCB_TP)(a0)
sd gp, (PCB_GP)(a0)
__fpe_state_save a0

findings.finding: cpu_throw() restores ra, sp, s[0-11], and conditionally FPE state from the new thread's pcb. No CHERI registers restored. The function path is consistent with the non-CHERI struct pcb layout.
findings.snippet:
ld ra, (PCB_RA)(x13)
ld sp, (PCB_SP)(x13)
ld s0, (PCB_S + 0 * 8)(x13)
...
__fpe_state_load x13

findings.finding: cpu_fork() copies PCB and trapframe via bcopy(..., sizeof(*pcb2)). sizeof(struct pcb) and sizeof(struct trapframe) are fixed at compile time for baseline RV64. In a CHERI kernel, struct pcb would need conditional sizeof based on the capability encoding width, but this tree is non-CHERI so the fixed size is correct.
findings.snippet:
bcopy(td1->td_pcb, pcb2, sizeof(*pcb2));
bcopy(td1->td_frame, tf, sizeof(*tf));

findings.finding: bhyve/vmm guest register set defines only standard RV64 GPRs (RA, SP, GP, TP, T0-T6, S0-S11, A0-A7, SEPC) as uint64_t values. No CHERI capability registers (PCC, DDC, CSP, CGP, CTP) are enumerated, and no per-register capability metadata/tag fields exist. Guest capability state is not virtualized because the kernel targets baseline RV64, not CHERI.

__register_t = __int64_t. On CHERI platforms this would need to be at minimum a 128/256-bit capability type to hold both address and metadata. The 64-bit definition confirms this is a baseline RV64 port. The user-visible ABI types (struct reg, struct gpregs, mcontext_t) derived from __register_t are internally consistent: they are all non-CHERI, so no cross-context-switch encoding mismatch can occur.
